claims.text:
Vinyarion is a Quenya name. Its meaning is not glossed, but Paul Strack suggests that it means "New Son" and is a compound of vinya ("new") and the suffix ion ("son").
Hyarmendacil is a Quenya name. It means "South-victor". It is a compound of hyarmen ("south") and -(n)dacil ("victor").
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "Gondor and the Heirs of Anárion", entry for king Ciryaher, p. 1045

claims.text: Vinyarion ascended the throne after his father Aldamir was killed in a battle with the Harad and the Corsairs of Umbar in . Eleven years later, in , he defeated the Men of the Harad and took the name Hyarmendacil II.

claims.text:
In a late manuscript of what would later become Appendix A, it is mentioned that Vinyarion took the name Hyarmendakil II in 1551 after a great victory over Harad in revenge for the death of his father Aldamir.
